title: 2015 HMMT February Geometry Problem 6
statement: In triangle \(A B C, A B=2, A C=1+\sqrt{5}\), and \(\angle C A B=54^{\circ}\). Suppose \(D\) lies on the extension of \(A C\) through \(C\) such that \(C D=\sqrt{5}-1\). If \(M\) is the midpoint of \(B D\), determine the measure of \(\angle A C M\), in degrees.

solutions.text: 63 Let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{A D} . E C=\sqrt{5}+1-\sqrt{5}=1\), and \(E M=1\) by similar triangles \((A B D \sim E M D) . \triangle E C M\) is isosceles, with \(m \angle C E M=54^{\circ}\). Thus \(m \angle A C M=m \angle E C M=\) \(\frac{180-54}{2}=63^{\circ}\).
